([[Brentwood, Tennessee]]) | college = [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] (2018–2019) | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2018) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2018) * 3× [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] (2016–2018) }} '''Darius Garland''' (born January 26, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). He is projected by many sports analysts as a [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] pick for the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Sparks|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2019/01/22/nba-draft-vanderbilt-basketball-darius-garland/2651731002/|title=Darius Garland to enter NBA draft|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=January 22, 2019|accessdate=January 24, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Projected NBA lottery pick Darius Garland withdraws from Vanderbilt to prepare for NBA Draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/projected-nba-lottery-pick-darius-garland-withdraws-from-vanderbilt-to-prepare-for-nba-draft/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |accessdate=February 3, 2019 |date=January 23, 2019}} Born in [[Gary, Indiana]] as the son of former basketball player [[Winston Garland]], Garland attended [[Brentwood Academy]] in high school. He joined the varsity basketball team in eighth grade and left as a four-time state champion and three-time [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] winner. He was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], ranked among the best [[point guard]]s in the 2018 class, and a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]. Garland committed to Vanderbilt as the best recruit in program history. After five games, his college career was cut short by a [[Tear of meniscus|meniscus injury]], which prompted him to leave the team to prepare for the NBA draft. ==Early life== Garland was born in [[Gary, Indiana]] to Felicia Garland and basketball player [[Winston Garland]]. He grew up playing [[baseball]] and started basketball at age five but soon narrowed down his focus to only the latter sport.{{cite web |title=Darius Garland |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/g/garland-darius-1.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=January 2, 2019 |date=March 13, 2018}} Garland continued with basketball in elementary school and scored his first basket in second grade.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Darius Garland is Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2016/04/17/darius-garland-boys-basketball-player-year/82668248/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=January 3, 2019 |date=April 17, 2016}} In third grade, he attended basketball camps in [[Valparaiso, Indiana]] led by [[Bryce Drew]], who would become his college coach at [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]].{{cite web |last1=Rexrode |first1=Joe |title=Darius Garland, Rick Byrd and an epic day for Nashville basketball |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2017/11/14/darius-garland-rick-byrd-and-epic-day-nashville-basketball/861176001/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=January 25, 2019 |date=November 14, 2017}} Garland played on a travel team against older opponents and joined an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) squad based in [[Nashville, Tennessee]] when he was in fourth grade, because none of the local teams met his standards.{{cite web |last1=Hutton |first1=Mike |title=Gary's Darius Garland turns into Brentwood's latest basketball savant |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/columnists/ct-ptb-mike-hutton-column-st-0129-20170128-column.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=January 27, 2019 |date=January 28, 2017}} After he completed sixth grade, his family moved to Tennessee so that he could attend [[Brentwood Academy]] in [[Brentwood, Tennessee]] with his AAU teammates Gavin Schoenwald and Camron Johnson.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Darius Garland of Brentwood Academy commits to Vanderbilt basketball |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/11/13/report-brentwood-academys-darius-garland-commits-vanderbilt/815173001/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=January 25, 2019 |date=November 13, 2017}} Garland's father described, "We had always talked about relocating. My mother had lived in Tennessee and she liked it. I just talked to the family and everybody was on board. It was a big leap of faith." ==High school career== Garland joined the starting lineup for the Brentwood Academy [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball team while in eighth grade.{{cite web |last1=Pulliam |first1=Charles |title=Brentwood Academy standout Garland chooses Vanderbilt |url=http://www.williamsonherald.com/sports/article_0f76026a-c8c0-11e7-ad01-0b42709ac4e7.html |website=Williamson Herald |accessdate=January 27, 2019 |date=November 13, 2017}} In his freshman season, he averaged 13 [[point (basketball)|points]], 1.3 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 2.7 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] per game, leading his team to a [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association]] (TSSAA) Division II-AA state championship.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=BA's Darius Garland named to USA Junior National Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/bas-darius-garland-named-to-usa-junior-national-team |website=''[[USA Today|''USA Today'' High School Sports]]'' |accessdate=January 27, 2019 |date=April 23, 2015}} Garland was one of three finalists for [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] among Division II-AA players.{{cite web |title=TSSAA’s Division II Mr. and Miss Basketball are announced |url=https://www.columbiadailyherald.com/sports/preps/tssaa-s-division-ii-mr-and-miss-basketball-are-announced |website=[[Daily Herald (Columbia, Tennessee)|Daily Herald]] |accessdate=January 27, 2019 |date=March 1, 2015}} On December 23, 2015, as a sophomore, he claimed [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors at the King of the Bluegrass Holiday Classic, after scoring 23 points versus [[Fairdale High School]] in the title game.{{cite web |last1=Frakes |first1=Jason |title=King of the Bluegrass: Brentwood Academy beats Trinity for title |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/king-of-the-bluegrass-brentwood-academy-beats-trinity-for-title |website=''[[USA Today|''USA Today'' High School Sports]]'' |accessdate=January 27, 2019 |date=December 23, 2015}} Garland averaged 18.6 points and 4.3 assists per game and earned TSSAA Division II-AA Mr. Basketball accolades. High school sports website [[MaxPreps]] also included him in its Sophomore All-American Team honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Hickman |first1=Jason |title=2015-16 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/FNPGNr8ro0KhVZ-LBt_WIQ/2015-16-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=January 27, 2019 |date=April 20, 2016}} From his sophomore to junior year, he grew 2½ inches, and by his fourth season with Brentwood Academy, he was ranked the best [[point guard]] in the 2018 class by [[college recruiting|recruiting]] service [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Nation's top junior point guard Darius Garland still yet to reach his peak |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/nations-top-junior-point-guard-darius-garland-still-yet-to-reach-his-peak |website=''[[USA Today|''USA Today'' High School Sports]]'' |accessdate=January 27, 2019 |date=January 5, 2017}} In March 2017, Garland garnered [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith Trophy]] High School All-America honorable mention recognition.{{cite web |title=Naismith Trophy High School Boys All-America team announced |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/naismith-trophy-high-school-boys-all-america-team-announced |website=''[[USA Today|''USA Today'' High School Sports]]'' |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=March 8, 2017}} He averaged 23.4 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.1 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game and led his team to a 30–2 record and state championship. Garland additionally earned MaxPreps Junior All-American first team distinction.{{cite web |title=2016-17 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/otwRLm_KeEGHwC460kRRPg/2016-17-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=April 11, 2017}} On November 13, 2017, he committed to play college basketball for Vanderbilt, drawn there by its proximity to his home and head coach Bryce Drew. Entering his senior season, Garland appeared in the [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA]] preseason team.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=2017-18 American Family Insurance ALL-USA Preseason Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/2017-18-american-family-insurance-all-usa-preseason-boys-basketball-team |website=''[[USA Today|''USA Today'' High School Sports]]'' |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=November 27, 2017}} He averaged 27.6 points, 5.0 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.7 steals and secured a fourth straight state title for Brentwood Academy, tying the TSSAA record.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/vpYHC6-v2kiq_nCltCL9_Q/2017-18-maxpreps-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team-.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=April 10, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Darius Garland |url=https://vucommodores.com/404-1.aspx?url=/roster.aspx?rp_id=4300 |publisher=[[Vanderbilt University]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20181015114521/https://vucommodores.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4300 |archivedate=October 15, 2018}} Garland joined the MaxPreps High School All-American third team and became the only player other than [[Brandan Wright]] to win Tennessee Mr. Basketball on three occasions. In March 2018, he was named Gatorade Tennessee Player of the Year and a semifinalist for the Naismith Trophy.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Michael |title=Vanderbilt signee Darius Garland named Gatorade Tennessee Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/08/darius-garland-named-gatorade-tennessee-boys-basketball-player-year/407831002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=March 8, 2018}} On March 28, Garland recorded a game-high 11 assists at the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018 McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web |title=Darius Garland has stellar McDonald's Game |url=https://vucommodores.com/news/2018/3/29/Darius_Garland_has_stellar_McDonald_amp_8217_s_Game.aspx?path=mbball |publisher=[[Vanderbilt University]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=March 29, 2018}} He took part in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] as well. {{College athlete recruit }} ==College career== Garland entered the [[2018–19 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|2018–19 season]] as the best recruit to ever sign with Vanderbilt.{{cite web |last1=Boclair |first1=David |title=Garland quickly establishes himself as VU's leader |url=https://www.nashvillepost.com/sports/vanderbilt-basketball/blog/21027995/garland-quickly-establishes-himself-as-vus-leader |website=[[NashvillePost.com]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=October 18, 2018}} He was the only freshman in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) to make the preseason all-conference team.{{Cite web|url=https://vucommodores.com/news/2018/11/6/mens-basketball-darius-garland-named-as-second-team-preseason-all-sec-selection.aspx|title=Darius Garland named as Second-Team Preseason All-SEC selection - Vanderbilt University|publisher=[[Vanderbilt University]]|language=en|access-date=November 9, 2018}} On November 6, 2018, in his first college game against [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]], Garland led all scorers with 24 points.{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401082918|title=Winthrop vs. Vanderbilt - Box Score - November 6, 2018 - ESPN|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=November 9, 2018}} In a 79–70 win over [[Liberty Flames men's basketball|Liberty]] on November 19, he scored a season-high 33 points, the second-most points by a freshman in school history.{{cite web |last1=Sparks |first1=Adam |title=How Darius Garland's 33 points nearly broke Vanderbilt record in his fourth game |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2018/11/19/vanderbilt-basketball-darius-garland-bryce-drew-liberty/1968914002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=November 19, 2018}} Garland injured his knee during a [[layup]] versus [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State]] on November 23 and left the game early.{{cite web |title=Vanderbilt Star Freshman Darius Garland Injured in Loss to Kent State |url=https://www.si.com/2018/11/23/ap-bkc-kent-state-vanderbilt |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=November 23, 2018}} Four days later, Vanderbilt head coach [[Bryce Drew]] revealed that Garland would be sidelined for the remainder of the season with a [[tear of meniscus|meniscus injury]].{{Cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25391948/vanderbilt-commodores-pg-darius-garland-miss-rest-season-meniscus-injury-left-knee|title=Vanderbilt's Darius Garland out for remainder of season|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=November 27, 2018 |accessdate=November 27, 2018}} On January 22, 2019, he announced that he would leave Vanderbilt to recover from his injury and prepare for the [[2019 NBA draft]]. Garland later became one of 77 total invitees to take part in the [[NBA Draft Combine]].[https://www.nba.com/article/2019/05/08/66-players-attend-nba-draft-combine Sixty-six players expected to attend NBA Draft Combine] However, he left the event early on May 15, with the notion that he got promised a selection by a team in the NBA draft lottery.[https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/nba-draft-2019-darius-garland-fuels-lottery-speculation-by-leaving-combine/wtjvwq3vvty11stf70mx6aptg NBA Draft 2019: Darius Garland fuels lottery speculation by leaving combine] ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] | 5 || 5 || 27.8 || .537 || .478 || .750 || 3.8 || 2.6 || .8 || .4 || 16.2 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Garland's father [[Winston Garland]] played [[college basketball]] for [[Missouri State Bears men's basketball|Missouri State]] before spending seven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{cite web |title=Five Things to Know: Darius Garland |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/03/hsum-features-garland.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=January 2, 2019 |date=March 17, 2018}} He later became a recreational leader at the [[Indiana State Prison]] and coach for [[West Side Leadership Academy]] in Gary.{{cite web |title=Winston Garland |url=https://www.nwitimes.com/winston-garland/article_374e1dfb-e5d7-5442-ab12-9c7abd4057ae.html |website=[[The Times of Northwest Indiana]] |accessdate=January 2, 2019 |date=September 30, 2015}} Both of Garland's grandfathers served in the [[United States Army]]. He has an older sister, Kacie, and older brothers, Desmond, Kody, Miguel{{Cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/10/12/darius-garland-brentwood-academy-star-guard-gears-up-season-his-recruitment-winds-down/731261001/|title=Darius Garland, Brentwood Academy's star guard, gears up for season as his recruitment winds down|website=The Tennessean|language=en|access-date=2019-04-10}} and Hilton. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/g/garland-darius-1.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Garland, Darius}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Indiana]] [[Category:Basketball players from Tennessee]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Gary, Indiana]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Nashville, Tennessee]] [[Category:Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball players]]
